title: Pass by lvalue reference
recap: Pass by non-const lvalue reference lets a function intentionally change caller-owned objects. The signature communicates that mutation is possible.
Two references can alias the same object. Prefer a simple temporary during swapping rather than relying on arithmetic tricks that break under aliasing or overflow.
objectives: Implement the stated behavior for multiple inputs.
Run the visible tests and explain one boundary case.
warnings: The function/type interface is fixed, but implementation syntax is your choice.
Do not remove the visible tests; the checker keeps an independent copy.
Respect the stated input domain and lifetime/range rules.
challenge: Implement sortPair(first,second), modifying the caller so first <= second. Swap only when necessary. If both reference parameters refer to the same integer, leave that integer unchanged. Values fit int; do not use arithmetic swapping that could overflow.
hints: Only swap when the first value is greater.
Save the first value before overwriting it.
Ordinary assignment through each reference updates the caller.
